why: Saunders is a rank-and-file officer in Fisk's own task force who later works to bring Fisk down, but no scene shows the two dealing, and the rules do not settle whether a leader and one low-level member of his force count as knowing each other.

The tie stays for now: Mace deals with Ward only inside the Framework, where Ward is a digital copy of a dead man, and the rules don't say whether a simulated version counts as knowing the real person.
Hernandez never meets Rawlins alive; he pushes the CIA to give Rawlins up and later sees his corpse, so it sits between knowing about an investigation target and the huge-consequences exception.
Valentina was presumably CIA director while Ross was president, which suggests they dealt with each other, but nothing on screen shows them together and her speech to Congress only cites him.

They are direct opponents in the Battle of Paris and each wiki page lists the other as an enemy, but it is unclear whether Wanda deals with the London Master himself or only with the whole group, so it sits on the shared-battle line.
Zola hints that Hydra arranged the crash that killed Maria, which would fit the huge-consequences exception, but his own part is only implied and never shown.
